framing_style.description: Locked-off single-camera stream capture (bedroom setup: red gaming chair, prize wheel on a stand, phone, hanging shirts). ALL framing change is instantaneous and DIGITAL - crops of one static source. Proof: (a) within every shot the ORB similarity to its own first frame is s=0.9967-1.0189 and rot=-0.11 to +0.28 deg, translation under 40 px at 1080 over spans up to 4.25 s (measured %/s: -0.23 to +1.13, i.e. no ramp - the only outlier, S1 at -3.19 %/s, is a 0.28 s shot where the total change is 0.9%); (b) across cuts rot is +0.02 to +0.43 deg with several boundaries a pure horizontal jump at s=1.000 (2.283 s: s=1.0026 tx=+94 px; 5.283 s: s=1.0026 tx=+493 px; 18.750 s: s=1.0003 tx=-162 px); (c) framing returns to exact identity across cuts and seconds apart (shot10 vs shot11 s=1.0014 rot=+0.43 tx=+3 ty=-15 px, 607 inliers; shot8 vs shot11 s=0.9996 rot=+0.026); (d) the uploader's 'LXST' watermark stays pinned to the identical screen position in every framing while the picture behind it scales - it is composited over the reframe, so the reframe is digital. Zoom ladder measured against the base framing (shots 8-11 = 1.00x): shots 4-6 = 1.10-1.13x (388 and 158 inliers, rot < 0.25 deg), shot 7 = 1.21-1.32x, shots 1-3 = ~1.40x. Punch-in is a hard cut to a new crop, never an animated push. No shake, no pan, no drift, no speed ramp observed.

caption.position: horizontally centred, vertically centred at 50.0% of frame height. Measured text-box centre on five clean cards: 49.72, 50.14, 49.93, 50.03, 50.35% (mean 50.03, spread 0.6%). Cap band spans 46.0-54.3% of height; glyph height 7-8% of frame height (~100-120 px at 1440). Horizontal centre 48.9-50.7% of width.
caption.style_description: Heavy geometric sans, ALL CAPS, some cards oblique/italic and some upright. Fill is a light tint of the card's hue (near-white core), carrying a thin bright white inner outline and a strong coloured outer neon glow/bloom. No opaque card background, no box, no hard black outline. Cards are very short - roughly 28 cards in 24 s, most 0.10-0.40 s. Action/annotation cards are wrapped in asterisks and get blinking asterisk sparkles (*SPINNING*, *HANG UP*).
caption.color: Per-card colour, cycling the whole hue circle rather than encoding anything: measured glow hues include green 90-120 deg, spring/cyan 160-180 deg, azure/blue 198-244 deg, violet 264 deg, magenta/pink 294-331 deg, red 2-24 deg, yellow 46-74 deg. Speaker test: only ONE speaker exists - Speed is alone on camera and the phone panel reads 'Cristiano Ronaldo / No Answer' then 'Calling...', i.e. Ronaldo never picks up and never speaks (that is the clip's joke). Colour therefore cannot and does not track a speaker; it is per-card emphasis, with one thematic block where the entire *HANG UP* run (16.85-23.35 s) is red to match the red-graded section.
caption.outline: thin white inner outline plus a large soft coloured outer neon glow; no opaque card, no drop shadow box
caption.animation: Per-card HORIZONTAL MOTION-BLUR SMEAR-IN, not a scale pop. Stepped at 60 fps on the ONE->MORE swap (n=1234-1249): outgoing card fades out over a single frame (n1237), the incoming card appears at +0 already at full size but smeared horizontally into unreadable streaks (n1238), resolves over 4 frames (n1238-1241, 67 ms) and is fully sharp with the glow settled by +6 frames (100 ms). Bright-core width measured across three cards gives 0.95 of settled at +0, a 1.02 peak at +2 frames (+33 ms) and 1.00 by +6 frames - that +/-2% is bloom shrinking as the blur resolves, not a scale ramp. START SCALE 1.00 (full size on frame 1), PEAK 1.02 at +2 frames, NO undershoot, settled by 100 ms. This clip does NOT follow the ~1.05-at-+5-frames (+83 ms) convention measured on three siblings, and it is not a per-word scale-in either: the whole card's bounding box is present at +0 (DREAM: x0=303, x1=757 on the very first frame).

effects: whip / zoom motion-blur transitions covering 6 cuts: 183 ms (11 f) at 0.350, 7.717, 15.117; 200 ms (12 f) at 16.850; 217 ms (13 f) at 22.017; 433 ms (26 f) at 23.350-23.617

full-frame RED colour flash + red-graded section: enters at 16.850 and again at 22.017; framing measured identical across both (s=0.9956/1.0022, tx=+2.3/-3.5 px, 303 and 151 ORB inliers) so these two are EFFECTS, not cuts
heavy grade: crushed blacks, very high saturation and strong sharpening/clarity - the whole clip has an over-processed HDR look
caption neon glow + blinking asterisk sparkles
letter-scatter / flying-letters text effect on the 'MY GOD' card around 7.88-8.05 s
broken-heart emoji sticker composited on his chest from ~23.6 s to the end (matches the title emoji)
channel watermark 'LXST' pinned bottom-left at ~54% height, semi-transparent, present in every frame and NOT affected by the reframes

NO vignette (p99 luma flat at 246-255 from frame centre to corner on a bright frame), no zoom lines, no chromatic aberration beyond the sharpening halo, no progress bar, no meme cutaway, no arrows/circles, no borders, no added grain
hook: Opens already mid-shout: Speed leaning into the lens screaming, ~1.40x punched in, with the caption 'CHAT' already burnt in on frame 1 - no title card, no build. The first cut lands at 0.350 s (a 183 ms whip-blur) and five caption cards fire in the first 1.8 s (CHAT / LISTEN / THIS / IS A / DREAM). Audio starts at its loudest of the whole clip (-6.8 dBFS RMS in the first 100 ms). The hook is pure energy plus the promise in the words: he is about to spin a wheel to decide who he calls.
audio: Raw stream audio, no music for the first two thirds. EBU R128: integrated -13.0 LUFS, LRA 6.0 LU, true peak -0.0 dBFS (clipping the ceiling). No continuous music bed early - quiet passages fall to -39 dBFS with no sustained low-frequency content (7.3-7.7 s: -25 dBFS; 15.0-15.13 s: -39 dBFS). A bass-heavy music/sting bed fades IN at ~16.5 s and runs to ~23.5 s under the 'HANG UP' section: 40-160 Hz energy sits 10-28 dB above the 300 Hz-3 kHz band there, versus roughly parity or below earlier. The editor ducks audio into several cuts - at 15.117 s the track falls to -54.8 dBFS (digital silence, impossible for live stream audio) for several frames then jumps to -12.9 dBFS on the new shot; similar fade-then-slam at 0.350 and 7.717. No sfx stingers on the cuts themselves; the loudness jumps are the incoming shot's own audio.
notes: COMPLETE. Prior mechanical claim of ZERO cuts is wrong - there are 10 verified cuts (24.7/min). Raw masked-MAD counts (caption band 40-66% masked, 270x360 luma): 6 events >0.10, ZERO >0.20, ZERO >0.35. Scene detection is blind here for exactly the reason warned about: the camera is locked off, so a cut leaves the background pixel-identical and only the crop changes. Channels used to build the verified list: (1) per-frame high-frequency energy normalised by a +/-45-frame local median - every edit point carries a deliberate blur transition, giving 12 clean events at ratio <0.72 plus a 13th at relaxed threshold; (2) masked MAD with +/-40-frame local-median normalisation; (3) ORB similarity across every candidate on labelled pre/post pairs, which separated real framing changes from effect-only events; (4) the physical prize wheel used as a rotation clock - it turns a steady -0.75 deg/frame (-45 deg/s) either side of the 7.717 s transition and the measured jump across the blur is -13.75 deg against -8.6 deg expected, i.e. under 0.15 s of removed time, so 7.717 s is a splice with no material time gap; (5) audio fade-to-silence at edit points (-54.8 dBFS at 15.117 s). THREE of the 13 transition events are EFFECTS, NOT CUTS, and are excluded from cut_times_s: 8.583 s (1-frame flash, framing s=0.9992 with 554 ORB inliers, wheel angle identical either side), 16.850 s and 22.017 s (red colour flashes, framing s=0.9956 and 1.0022 with 303 and 151 inliers, subject pose continuous). One cut carries NO blur at all - 2.283 s is a hard jump cut proven only by geometry: a background-only match gives s=1.0012, rot=+0.057, tx=+95 px at 1080 against same-shot controls of -1.4 and +7.1 px. WHAT I COULD NOT DETERMINE: (a) whether the same-framing cuts at 0.350, 7.717 and 23.350 s remove any source time - the camera is locked so framing cannot tell, the wheel clock bounds 7.717 at under 0.15 s, and no clock exists at 0.350 or 23.350; they are counted as cuts because each carries the same deliberate blur transition and audio fade as the framing-changing cuts. (b) The zoom-ladder values above 1.13x (shot 7 measured 1.21x and 1.32x by two routes) are uncertain to about +/-10% because the physically-rotating wheel contaminates ORB and the mask that removes it also removes most of the usable features. (c) Words-per-card 1.2 is estimated from reading ~28 cards off the sheets, not from OCR. SINGLE-SOURCE REPRODUCIBLE: the phone showing the FaceTime UI is the real physical phone in the room (visible perspective, screen reflections, ambient light), not a composited second input, so nothing here needs an extra filtergraph input except the LXST watermark and the broken-heart emoji sticker. Genuine 60 fps - mpdecimate keeps 1457/1457 frames, so this is NOT 30 duplicated into 60.
